title: Review cadence affects detection delay independently of review count
problem: How should fixed periodic review opportunities be spaced when a formerly valid rule can become unsuitable after an unknown change?
failure: Clustered inspections leave long blind intervals. A current failure without historical ground truth also cannot distinguish an original defect from a subsequent change.
correction: In the uniform-phase persistent-defect model with independent equal sensitivity, cyclic mechanical gaps floor((i+1)T/m)-floor(iT/m) minimize mean detection delay. Equal gaps attain the lower bound (T/m)*(2-s)/(2*s)-1/2 when m divides T. Preserve historical evaluation conditions separately from current results.
transfer: Distinguish coverage, detection quality, cadence and temporal provenance. Validate dependence, persistence and onset assumptions before designing an actual review schedule.
limits: Periodic integer calendar, uniform onset phase, persistent defect, constant independent sensitivity s>0, no false positives, equal audit count, mean delay objective. 312 period/rate cases and 16380 exact composition comparisons. No production policy change, empirical measurement, originality or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
